title: Universal scope and risk
explanation: The failure-prevention rules that are fact-shaped: a change outside the declared scope, an unlabeled assumption, a risky change without a fallback, and an operation on off-limits content.

cases.original: Change only what the task requires: the declared scope, and nothing beyond it.
cases.note: A change with no matching task_scope fact is out of scope; the extractor supplies both.
cases.suggestion: Say "every changed path has an operation line in the task".

cases.original: When an ambiguity cannot change the output, scope, or safety, proceed and state the assumption in the output.
cases.note: The extractor marks whether the assumption is labeled in the output; the rule refuses an unlabeled one.
cases.suggestion: Say "state every assumption as an assumption in the output".

cases.original: Before changing a system through its only access path, stage a fallback: a backup, a rollback point, or a second access path.
cases.note: The extractor records whether a fallback exists; whether it is adequate is a judgement.
cases.suggestion: Name the fallback kind the task stages (backup, rollback point, or second path).

cases.original: Leave off-limits content untouched: no introspection, indexing, backup, summary, or reference.
cases.note: The rule joins an off-limits path to an operation on it; the wider meaning (index, summarise, reference) is a review.
cases.suggestion: Name the off-limits paths in a list the extractor can read.
